item.title: Guenther Steiner warns George Russell: Do not "poke the bear" Max Verstappen
item.description: Motorsport photo Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner has urged Mercedes driver George Russell not to "poke the bear" with Max Verstappen , after their war of words at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Russell hit out at Verstappen after the pair clashed in final practice, saying the Red Bull driver walks around "like they're bigger and better than everyone else" and that "somebody's got to stand up to that guy". The pair then swapped the lead repeatedly during the race on the Las Vegas Strip, until the Briton locked up and hit the wall on lap 48 while trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second. Verstappen won, and afterwards said Russell was "so far below my level" . Speaking on The Red Flags Podcast , Steiner said he did not mind the two drivers disliking each other, but questioned why Russell had chosen to take Verstappen on. "No, I mean, I haven't got a problem with it, because in the end, if they don't like each other, what do I care?" Steiner said. "This has been going on for a long time between them, and obviously, George coming out to say, 'Oh, this guy behaves very arrogantly', or whatever he said about Max, and 'Somebody needs to stand up to him.' Yeah, good luck with that one, buddy. You see how that worked out." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes The former team chief said he respected Russell as a driver, but felt he had underestimated Verstappen's mental strength. "I respect George as a race car driver, but in the end, Max is just mentally superior. On how to manage mental things, he's so superior to you, do not poke the bear, in my opinion," he said. "There is no need for it, because you don't do yourself any favours. Get over it. Try to win races instead of picking a battle with the best driver out there, the strongest mental guy out there, because guess what? You're going to lose. "It's like there's nobody sitting down with him and saying, 'George, sometimes less is more. Just say nothing, do your own job,'" Steiner said, adding that the Mercedes driver should focus on winning races. "And then when you have got something to say because you beat the guy, pick your battle then. But as I said, if you cannot beat them, join them, and in the moment just shut up and get on with it." Verstappen's win moved him further clear in second place in the drivers' standings on 304 points. Russell, who finished ninth, is fourth on 264, behind Lewis Hamilton . item.title: Nonbinary athletes sue Philadelphia Marathon over unequal treatment in race categories
item.description: Three nonbinary runners sued Philadelphia and its marathon race director Tuesday over a rule that requires athletes to register as male or female to compete in the elite fields at the city’s marathon and half marathon. Winter Parts, Reed Williams and Miche Palmer, who use they/them pronouns, are asking a judge to order race organizers to end what the runners say is discrimination under the city’s Fair Practices Ordinance. They filed the suit against the city and race director Kathleen Titus in Philadelphia’s Court of Common Pleas, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported . At the Philadelphia Marathon on Sunday, runners could register as nonbinary in the open division, where they started in corrals behind the elite field. The difference extends to the finish line. When Williams won the nonbinary open division in 2024, they received $4,000. The men’s and women’s elite winners each earned $10,000, according to the lawsuit. “The hope is that this will be equal across the board in the future,” Parts told Philadelphia ABC affiliate WPVI . The city told the station it does not comment on pending litigation. Related : These trans and nonbinary candidates just made history Other local races already offer what the runners are seeking. The Philadelphia Distance Run offers an elite nonbinary category with equal prize money. The Independence Blue Cross Broad Street Run added one this year. Parts won it. The runners filed a complaint with the Philadelphia Commission on Human Relations in 2025. This year, the commission issued a right-to-sue notice, clearing the way for the runners to take their case to court. By the time the runners filed the complaint, local LGBTQ+ running groups had been pressing the city for a change for two years. Josh Fernandez, a nonbinary runner who was then executive director of Philadelphia-based Queer Run, told the Philadelphia Gay News in 2025 that city officials pointed to the sport’s governing body when advocates asked them to add an elite nonbinary category. “The governing bodies don’t manage the prize money. That’s managed by the people who manage the race, and the race is owned by the City of Philadelphia,” Fernandez said, adding that a third category would leave the men’s and women’s prizes intact. item.title: Karson Milbrandt’s 29% Strikeout Rate Sparks Rule-5 Buzz
item.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect During the 2026 Double-A season, Karson Milbrandt fanned close to 40% of batters he encountered. This dominant performance earned him a spot as the No. 70 prospect in Just Baseball’s August Top 100 update. Yet the Miami Marlins left him unprotected on the 40-man roster when the deadline passed on Tuesday. This move signals a major risk for a pitcher whose numbers looked unstoppable just months ago. A Tale of Two Seasons Milbrandt’s season splits tell a story of rapid rise and sudden fall. In Double-A this year, his strikeout-minus-walk rate soared to 29.0% from a solid 16.7% in 2025. He relied on a fastball that averaged between 18 and 20 inches of induced vertical break in A-ball during the 2025 season, according to Just Baseball . That same pitch lost its life once he reached the highest minor league level. Per Just Baseball, his vertical break fell to just 16 inches in Triple-A last season. The loss of movement made his fastball easier to hit, even though the speed remained high. His control issues grew worse as the competition got tougher. Milbrandt could not stay in the zone with his off-speed pitches, which led to a spike in walks. His earned run average climbed from a microscopic 1.34 in Double-A to a disastrous 8.39 across 64.1 innings in Triple-A. The team that drafts him in the Rule-5 Draft will need to figure out why his stuff vanished so quickly. The Pitcher Heavy Draft The upcoming Rule-5 Draft is expected to be dominated by pitchers again. Since 2022, pitchers accounted for 44 of the 53 MLB phase selections. Front offices operated under the assumption that a lockout might cancel the draft entirely. This fear left many desirable names like Milbrandt vulnerable to being taken by another team. If the draft happens, the list of seven intriguing names from Just Baseball could see a massive shakeup. Teams will look to grab high-upside arms that got left behind due to roster crunches. Other pitchers on the watch list include Zach Franklin of the New York Mets. Franklin is viewed as a true reliever prospect who was part of a trade return. The lack of protection for these arms suggests teams are betting on their potential over their current results. According to Just Baseball analysis, a team is guaranteed to take a flier on Milbrandt. The real question remains about what went wrong and how to fix it. Looking Beyond the Marlins The situation in Miami highlights a broader trend in how teams handle young arms. The Marlins have a deep system, but they could not protect everyone before the deadline. This leaves fans wondering if they lost a future star or just exposed a flawed pitch. The data shows a clear drop in spin and command that needs immediate attention. If a new team can restore his vertical approach angle, his value could skyrocket. item.title: ‘That’s just wrong’: Draymond Green reacts to what people said right after Steph Curry’s injury
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors have finally won a game. Steve Kerr’s men went on an eight-game winning streak after their terrible start to the season, but they then lost each of their next five games. On Sunday, the Warriors returned to winning ways, beating the Celtics 88-87. One of the big reasons behind Golden State’s problems is the absence of Steph Curry, who has been out for a while now due to injury. Yaxel Lendeborg was tasked with replacing the Warriors’ talisman, but that expectation from people was just wrong, says Draymond Green. Draymond Green hits back at people expecting Yaxel Lendeborg to replace Steph Curry Lendeborg had such a good start to his NBA career when he was playing with Curry. The 24-year-old looked like a real force, and he was many people’s pick to win the Rookie of the Year award when he was firing on all cylinders. That form convinced many people that he could do a job for the Warriors no matter the circumstances, which is why some expected him to just fill Curry’s shoes after his injury. Lendeborg then went through a really rough run, which affected him. Green has now claimed that people should’ve never put him in that position. He said, as per Luca Evans on X : “First off is understanding that no one’s gonna be Steph. No one’s gonna slide into that role and all of a sudden become the greatest shooter to ever live, the greatest point guard to ever live, or a top-five player to ever live. That’s a tough role to slide into. “And so I think initially, as – with Steph going out, Yax, you can see him answering the questions like, ‘Yeah, I need to do this.’ And everybody’s like, ‘You know what, our second option, you need to slide in.’ And that’s just wrong. “And I’ve been here for 15 years – no one can replace Steph Curry. 15 years from now, no one will replace Steph Curry. He is one of one. “And so, then, it’s about, what do we need to do? And the reality is, come out and use each other. Use each other to create advantages.” Green is spot on. Expecting a rookie like Lendeborg, despite his incredible talent and potential, to seamlessly fill Curry’s shoes is absolutely absurd. Nobody can do that. The Warriors had to change their style to find a way to win without their main man, and they did that well against the Celtics. That is exactly what they need to keep doing until Curry is back in action. item.title: Tennessee fined $250,000 after fans took Josh Heupel’s golf ball suggestion against Lane Kiffin
item.description: Lane Kiffin’s second return to Neyland Stadium as a visiting head coach produced the same scene as his first, and on Sunday it produced the same response from the Southeastern Conference. With 3:14 left in No. 9 Tennessee’s 27-13 win over LSU on Saturday, play stopped after a pass interference call as fans in the student section sent golf balls and mustard bottles toward the LSU bench. Tigers players moved toward midfield to get out of range until the field was cleared. Tennessee Vols head coach Josh Heupel has been named in The Athletics rankings of the top 25 coaches in college football. Photo Credit: Tennessee Athletics The league fined Tennessee $250,000 under its sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies. That is the same amount, under the same policies, the SEC assessed in October 2021, when Kiffin brought Ole Miss to Knoxville and was hit by a golf ball during a 20-minute delay. As it did five years ago, the conference left alcohol sales in place and reserved the right to suspend them later. Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel set the tone for the rematch in July, when he was asked at SEC Media Days in Tampa about Kiffin’s first trip back to Knoxville as LSU’s coach. “Certainly hope our fanbase hasn’t cooled off, whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard or our sports stores making sure they’ve got reinforcements on the golf balls. Hopefully, Knoxville is ready for his arrival,” Heupel said . He called the remark a joke on the SEC coaches teleconference during game week. “That was a tongue-in-cheek comment at SEC Media Days. But we need our fans to be a part of this football game and create a tough environment on Saturday afternoon. I have no questions that our fans will be there early, will be hydrated and will be ready to compete for 60 minutes, too,” Heupel said. Why Kiffin was not surprised by the golf balls “Probably not when the coach says that at SEC Media Days, to go buy your golf balls. And I’m not being critical of him. I’m laughing at it. But they listened to their coach. So no, that doesn’t surprise me,” Kiffin said after the game. Sunday’s fine is Tennessee’s second fan-conduct penalty of the season. The SEC hit the school for $500,000 after fans stormed the field following an Oct. 17 win over then-No. 6 Alabama, money that went to the Crimson Tide under league policy. A week later, South Carolina owed the same amount for storming its own field after beating Tennessee, which effectively sent that half-million back to Knoxville. item.title: Marc Marquez: 'Curbing my instincts was key to winning 2026 MotoGP title'
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez says his 10th world championship title took more of a mental effort than any of his others. Marquez overturned a yawning 102-point deficit after an early-season injury absence to grab the crown in last weekend's Portuguese Grand Prix, with one round remaining. Riding with fitness limitations following his surgery in May, there were several weekends on which Marc was the not the fastest rider. But his ability to limit the damage in unfavourable situations and maximise points when he had an advantage proved decisive. Key to that strategy was avoiding mistakes - which in turn required the Spaniard to curb his racer's instinct to always go for victory. As Marquez explained after the race at Portimao, this was a psychological skill he developed during the course of 2026. "You know, this was the one [championship] that I worked more [the most] on my mental side. Because it was the only way. "I already understood that in the first part of the season, [my] instinct was not working anymore. "Always I want to win. You know, I'm a fighter, but I didn't feel that I must win, yes or yes. Because if you have that mentality in this championship, it was impossible to win. "This new Marc Marquez, new mentality, gives me the chance to finish races in seventh place,[or] fifth and take points. And yeah, of course, then at good circuits you need to win." Brad Binder, Red Bull KTM Factory Racing, Marco Bezzecchi, Aprilia Racing, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team He expanded on the theme at the subsequent press conference dedicated to his triumph. Asked if this was the title for which he had to show the most resilience and the toughest mentality, Marc agreed. "Yes. For that reason, I said [in the pre-event press conference last Thursday] this is the best [version of] Marc. Because the best athlete, I believe that arrives [an athlete reaches his best] when you can control yourself and when you can control your mental side. "And this year, I just worked on my mental side, because I understood that my physical condition was arriving one point [had hit a ceiling]. "And then I said, 'OK, give up, try to train in a normal way, try to, of course, do extra work with the physiotherapist, but work in a normal way.' "'What do I need? Braking, hauling the bike, and that's it. And try to be very fit.' "But especially, [I needed] to understand where it was possible and where it was not possible. And this was the main point." "Since I came back, I never crashed in a sprint or main race. Yesterday, yes - but it was a big warning." Marquez took that warning to heart on Sunday, riding even more carefully to bag an eighth place that was enough to become 2026 MotoGP champion. item.title: ‘Disgusting football’: Robert Saleh does not hold back on ’embarrassing’ Titans loss
item.description: Tennessee Titans Coach Robert Saleh talks with the media after the joint practice with the Seattle Seahawks at Vanderbilt Health Football Center Friday, Aug. 21, 2026. The Tennessee Titans’ defense got absolutely shredded by the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, as Dallas scored touchdowns on each of its first six drives on the way to a 51-30 win. It was the third straight game in which the Titans allowed at least 40 points. After the game, head coach Robert Saleh didn’t hold back. Saleh called his team’s defensive performance “disgusting” and “embarrassing,” adding that the blame for it “starts with me.” Titans’ Rough First Season Under Saleh Saleh’s first season in Tennessee has been a difficult one. The Titans opened the year with five straight losses, prompting the team’s CEO to issue an apology to fans . Tennessee finally got in the win column with a 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6. But the Titans haven’t won since, dropping to 1-9 with Sunday’s loss. The defense has been a big part of the problem. Tennessee allowed 43 points in an overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and 40 points in a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars before Sunday’s game in Dallas. According to ESPN, the Titans are now just the fourth team since the 1970 merger to allow 40 or more points in three consecutive games, joining the 1975 Cleveland Browns, the 1981 Baltimore Colts, and the 2004 Titans. ‘Disgusting football’ On Sunday, the Cowboys racked up 480 yards of total offense. Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards, and CeeDee Lamb had 132 receiving yards. Dallas scored on every drive except the last one, when it simply kneeled out the clock. It was a disastrous performance from the Titans, and when Saleh was asked what needs to change on defense after the loss, he gave a blunt answer. “There’s a lot of things that need to change. Obviously, it’s disgusting football. It’s embarrassing football. And obviously, that starts with me,” Saleh said, via the Titans . Saleh was then asked how he can call a game when nothing is working. “That’s why I get paid. I got to figure it out,” Saleh said. He also made it clear how he wants his players to feel about the performance. “I want to — hopefully, they feel pissed. Just feeling something,” Saleh said. When asked what part of the defense needs fixing the most, Saleh pointed to his players losing their individual matchups. “When I go back and watch this tape, I have a feeling I’m going to know exactly what it is. The NFL is a game of one-on-ones, and when you get a one-on-one, you’ve got to win your opportunities. And today, they won their opportunities, and we didn’t,” Saleh said. We’ll have to see how the team bounces back from this, but it’s pretty clear that Saleh was not impressed by the showing. item.title: Eastleigh for sale as Donald makes emotional statement
item.description: Stewart Donald was previously owner at Sunderland [Getty Images] Eastleigh owner Stewart Donald has revealed that he will leave the club at the end of the current season after recent personal tragedy alongside the rising costs of being in the National League. He first acquired the Spitfires15 years ago, stepping away for a brief spell when he joined Sunderland before returning to the Hampshire club in April 2023. Donald led a consortium which took over the Black Cats from Ellis Short in May 2018 before selling a controlling stake in 2021. He then reinvested further funds into Eastleigh during his second spell before announcing on Sunday that he would leave the Silverlake Stadium following a turbulent and tragic period in his personal life. "Before departing [for Sunderland] I ensured the club was financially stable by leaving over three million in the club's account," Donald said in an open letter. "Upon my return these funds had understandably been exhausted and it was a difficult time for the club, including me and in hindsight I perhaps should not have returned. "But I did not want the club to be relegated and the ground needed significant work so I invested a further £1m so the club could continue at the same level. "Around that time my wife was diagnosed with cancer at 36, we had a young family. My mother sadly passed away shortly before my wife, and my father was also diagnosed with terminal cancer. "I had to spend less time at the club than I hoped, despite this my commitment never waned and I continued to fully fund the club through this period." Eastleigh sit 16th in the National League, having played in the fifth tier since winning promotion in 2014. The club parted company with manager Matt Gray in mid-November and are yet to announce a new head coach, with former boss Richard Hill conducting post-match interviews after their 3-1 win over Tamworth on Saturday. Donald shared in his letter he was actively looking for a new buyer at the club, but was yet to receive any offers from serious candidates. "At the start of the season I made the decision that it would be my last," he added. "Sadly at the moment there have been no serious candidates. There have been many enquiries but they have no credentials or serious funds. "Eastleigh currently use all of its revenues to cover the ever increasing operational costs so any investor must be prepared to fund the entire first-team budget, as I currently do. "With around five months of the season remaining, the board will seek a meeting with the supporters group to discuss the future of the club in more detail." item.title: 'You don't win 345 matches by defending' - Simeone breaks La Liga record
item.description: Diego Simeone beat the record of Luis Aragones, who recorded his final La Liga victory in 2004 [Getty Images] Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club. Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight. Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total. "It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games. "I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this." Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face". He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it. "This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?" The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain. He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure. Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later. He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign. Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge. However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016. Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018. His contract expires at the end of this season with the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign. item.title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
item.description: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. item.title: The dangerous gamble Man United face in bid to escape a brutal reality
item.description: After wrestling with one season-defining dilemma for weeks, the Manchester United hierarchy might immediately face another following their latest humiliation at the hands of bitter rivals Liverpool . Do they spend the £150m they can just about get away with in a difficult January window, affecting future planning, or actually risk a future that is almost unimaginable: relegation. The weight of that decision is only made heavier by a much more difficult decision facing Mauricio Pochettino . What system does he go with? What approach can actually amplify the abilities of these players? What formation can get them out of this mess, and just steady things? Ideally, Pochettino would play his high-pressing system in a 4-3-3… but we’re a long way from ideals. We're into brutal realities. This squad just isn’t ready for that, and the manager faces yet another dilemma in how trying to prepare them for such an approach might bring a brutal learning period that only worsens an already dismal situation. They don’t have that luxury right now. But what is it ready for? What has it been built to? Mauricio Pochettino in discussion with Man United assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D'Agostino (Getty) One insider tells the Independent about yet another contradiction in its strange construction. They were bemoaning the quality of the centre-halves, one of the few areas where the squad is overstocked, but pointed to how the latter almost dictates that you have to lean on them. The urgency of the situation almost warrants Pochettino just going to a back five in a bid to grind out a few badly-needed wins. In other words, break glass for emergency. But then that’s where they are, an extreme situation that has incrementally been reached. It’s a bit like bankruptcy, an analogy that is by this point at bit too fitting: gradually then all at once. The state of the squad spells that out. As recently as five years ago, United were paying out one of the highest wage bills in football. Not all of it may have been worth it but the sheer expense offered a certain insulation. That insulation has frayed to the point of vanishing. The club’s financial situation, as they seek to service so much debt, has influenced and combined with the team’s lack of success to force their level - in quality and spending power - further and further down. item.title: JJ Redick Explains How Austin Reaves’ Absence Has Hurt The Lakers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Hui-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have gone 3-1 since Austin Reaves was sidelined with a heel injury, but while that record looks good, the performances haven’t been great. The Lakers have struggled a bit offensively without Reaves, and head coach JJ Redick spoke about the impact of his absence at Sunday’s practice . “The stat that stands out the most is like first 12 games, we were the No. 1 half-court offense,” Redick said, via Dave McMenamin. “Austin was on the court for 70% of those possessions. In the last seven games, we’ve not been a good half-court offense. Austin’s been on the court for 9% of those possessions. “So who would have thought that not having an elite offensive player, All-Star-level player, would hurt your offense?” Redick continued. “That’s crazy to me. It’s crazy. So, we’re going to be fine.” When Reaves is out, the Lakers have only one reliable shot creator in the half-court, Luka Doncic . Teams then have the option of keying in on Doncic, which is what the Sacramento Kings did on Friday. The Slovenian was constantly doubled, and his teammates didn’t always take advantage. The Lakers still won, but the score was 106-104 against the Kings, one of the worst teams in the NBA. This also happened just a couple of nights after the lowly Utah Jazz beat Redick’s men 109-97 on Wednesday. So, the Lakers definitely need Reaves back as soon as possible, but they won’t push him. In fact, Doncic told the 28-year-old to be cautious and take his time returning from this injury . Reaves suffered this left heel bruise in the Lakers’ 123-112 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 11. Redick was hopeful he’d return either against the Jazz on Monday or the San Antonio Spurs on Friday . Well, Reaves has been ruled out for that rematch with the Jazz, which means he is set to miss his sixth game of the season. Before suffering this heel injury, the undrafted guard had missed the 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 9 due to illness. The performances might not always have been great, but it’s commendable that the Lakers are 4-1 overall without Reaves, who has averaged 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game in 2026-27. They are tied for the best record in the NBA at 14-3 despite their second-best player having missed a fair bit of time early on. Redick deserves a lot of credit for the Lakers’ success. They were criticized for hiring him back in 2024, given he had never coached at even the high school level, but he has proven to be a great hire. Redick led the Lakers to back-to-back 50-win campaigns in his first two seasons. The 42-year-old looks set to pull that off in his third season at the helm as well, and not many have had this kind of start to their coaching careers.

item.description: The New England Patriots are expected to have interest in quarterback Daniel Jones following his release from the Indianapolis Colts , but a signing does not appear to be imminent. Instead, head coach Mike Vrabel continues to back Tommy DeVito as the Patriots’ starter with regular QB1 Drake Maye sidelined due to injury. “This is Day 1 of what we’re going to look like here going forward with Tommy,” Vrabel told WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. “We talked about [adding another quarterback]. I don’t think that that’s something that will happen today. But we’ll see. I don’t know that that’s something that we necessarily think. We have guys that have been with us, understand what we’re doing, and how we want to try to do it.” DeVito first arrived in New England as a waiver claim in August 2025, following his release from the New York Giants. He spent his first year with the club as the third-string quarterback behind Maye and Joshua Dobbs, and as a consequence saw no game action at any point throughout the season — a first in his three-year NFL career. Nonetheless, the Patriots were happy with DeVito’s development and signed him to a two-year, xx million contract extension in early March. Two weeks later, they released Dobbs. DeVito entered the 2026 regular season as the Patriots’ second-string quarterback between Maye and rookie Behren Morton, and as such appeared in two games before permanently taking over against the Detroit Lions in Week 10: when Maye suffered a broken fibula on the opening drive, New England turned to its backup. DeVito ended up completing 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each in a 35-10 loss. Now at 5-5, the Patriots are seemingly holding out hope for Maye to return at some point; he is reportedly expected to miss at least six weeks, which would leave the door open for a comeback down the stretch. For the time being, however, they are rallying behind DeVito. “We’ll see how he progresses and how long that takes,” Vrabel said about Maye. “I don’t think there’s any timetable right now. We’ll have to play and go here with ‘Two Chains’ and play good football, and find ways to win a game here.”

That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
